purpose: Local, dependency-light fallback tools for safe OOXML (.docx) editing when the meridian-docs MCP extension or a Word MCP tunnel slot is unavailable. Exists to satisfy Meridian's capability-manifest fallback_chain contract (AGENTS.md, 649e095f) as a documented, already-wired alternative -- never ad-hoc improvisation. Zero dependency on the Meridian server, its DB, any MCP tool, or Serena memories; source-of-truth is this tracked package plus durable PatchManifest pointers, per the originating proposal.

dependencies.note: python-docx is intentionally NOT used or required -- it is not a pypi-dependency of this repo's pixi environment (see pixi.toml), and this package must not require adding one. All OOXML handling is stdlib zipfile + xml.etree.ElementTree.

do_not: Do not edit the canonical thesis DOCX (or any other production document) directly with these tools outside of a reviewed PatchManifest + backed-up transaction.

Do not treat this package as a replacement for meridian-docs' stable-paragraph-ID navigation, captions, citations, bibliography, or equations -- see docs/docx-mcp-parity.md for the parity matrix between the Word MCP slot and meridian-docs.
Do not depend on Serena or editor memories for how these modules behave -- this file plus the tracked source under tools/meridian_fallbacks/ is the source of truth.
Do not delete or replace the pre-existing thesis temp_scripts prototype copies until parity with this tracked package is proven -- this package supersedes them in intent, not (yet) by removal.

supported_operations: re-exports the public API of every module below
PACKAGE_VERSION / SCHEMA_VERSION constants
limitations: Deliberately does NOT import output_provenance_gate or docx_completion_gate (see related_sprint_items d3374b0e / 8419f55f) -- import those submodules directly once they land.

supported_operations: read_parts_from_bytes(data) -> {part_name: bytes}
build_zip_bytes(parts) -> bytes (deterministic, sorted-name order)
verify_zip_bytes(data, required_parts=...) -> DocxValidationReport (real zip CRC check, required-part presence, well-formed-XML check on word/document.xml)
SafeOoxmlWriter.read_parts() / write_parts() / restore_backup() -- validate-then-backup-then-atomic-replace discipline (temp file in the same directory + fsync + os.replace)
compute_sha256(data) -> hex digest
limitations: Validates zip integrity, required-part presence, and word/document.xml well-formedness only -- this is NOT full OOXML schema validation.
Atomic replace relies on os.replace within the SAME directory/filesystem as the target -- a target directory that isn't a real filesystem path (e.g. some virtual/network mounts) is unsupported.
Backups accumulate on disk (one timestamped file per write) -- this module does not prune old backups; callers that write frequently should manage retention themselves.

supported_operations: compute_image_insert_parts(parts, image_bytes, image_ext=..., anchor_text=..., paragraph_index=..., width_emu=..., height_emu=...) -> ImageInsertResult (pure, in-memory)
insert_image(docx_path, image_path=... | image_bytes=..., ...) -> ImageInsertWriteResult (disk-touching, uses SafeOoxmlWriter)
build_drawing_xml(...) -> minimal valid inline <w:drawing> OOXML
supported image extensions: png, jpg/jpeg, gif, bmp, tif/tiff, emf, wmf
limitations: Never decodes or validates actual image content/dimensions -- treats image bytes as opaque, keyed only by file extension for the Content-Type mapping.

Locates insertion anchors via a targeted regex over word/document.xml's raw text (paragraph boundaries via `<w:p>`/`<w:p/>` splicing) rather than a full XML tree edit -- see safe_ooxml_writer.py's module docstring for why. Assumes document.xml has no literal `</w:p>`-shaped text inside a run (true for every real Word/python-docx-produced document; not schema-impossible in adversarial input).
anchor_text matching is a plain substring match against a paragraph's concatenated, tag-stripped text -- not a cross-run-aware phrase search and not case-insensitive.
Always inserts an INLINE drawing (wp:inline) -- floating/anchored (wp:anchor) image placement is not supported.

supported_operations: PatchManifest.create(...) / create_from_file(...) -- new draft manifest, optionally hashing the current on-disk target as base_sha256
PatchManifest.add_operation(kind, target_part, description, payload=..., metadata=...) -- kind in {replace_part, insert_image, custom}
PatchManifest.verify_base_unchanged(...) -- staleness check against the target's current hash
PatchManifest.to_dict()/to_json()/from_dict()/from_json() -- schema_version-checked (de)serialization
PatchManifest.save(path)/load(path) -- atomic JSON persistence (temp file + fsync + os.replace)
mark_applied()/mark_aborted(reason) -- terminal status transitions; only a 'draft' manifest accepts add_operation
limitations: Never embeds large binary payloads inline -- only a sha256 + byte size per operation. The real payload bytes must be supplied separately at apply time and are verified against the recorded hash.
from_dict()/from_json() reject any manifest whose schema_version does not exactly match PATCH_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION (currently 1) -- no automatic migration between schema versions.

supported_operations: apply_patch_manifest(manifest, payloads=..., allow_stale_base=False, dry_run=False, appliers=...) -> MergeResult -- all-or-nothing apply of every operation in a manifest
rollback(manifest, merge_result) -> WriteResult -- restore the target to its pre-apply state using the backup a successful apply created
DEFAULT_APPLIERS: {'replace_part': ..., 'insert_image': ...} -- extensible via the appliers= kwarg for custom operation kinds
limitations: dry_run=True is a pure preview: it never mutates manifest.status (success or failure), so a failed preview can be fixed and re-previewed without rebuilding the manifest. Only a real (non-dry-run) apply transitions a manifest out of 'draft'.

A stale base_sha256 raises MergeConflictError rather than auto-merging -- there is no 3-way merge; the caller must explicitly opt in via allow_stale_base=True or re-create the manifest against the current file.
Operations are applied strictly in the order they appear in manifest.operations -- no dependency graph or reordering.

supported_operations: check_output_provenance(outputs_dir, path, max_scan_files=200_000) -> dict -- the local fallback answer to 'what do we know about this output's provenance', ranked EXACT > STALE_BY_SCRIPT > DIRECTORY_FALLBACK > UNREGISTERED > UNKNOWN

Explicit provenance_type statuses (string-identical to extensions/meridian-outputs/meridian_outputs/provenance_status.py's own constants): EXACT='exact', DIRECTORY_FALLBACK='directory_fallback', UNREGISTERED='unregistered', UNKNOWN='unknown', STALE_BY_SCRIPT='stale_by_script'
ScanState -- one snapshot of this call's bounded outputs_dir scan (generation/converged/scanned_count/truncated/errors/scanned_at); gates the 'inconclusive' field
main(argv) -- CLI entry point: `python output_provenance_gate.py <outputs_dir> <path>`, exit 0/2
limitations: Reads the SAME on-disk ledgers the real meridian-outputs extension writes (<outputs_dir>/.meridian-outputs-cache/{provenance_ledger.json,fingerprint_ledger.json}, plus MERIDIAN_NOTES.md) via plain json.load/file reads -- never imports meridian_outputs, duckdb, or xxhash.

Its own file-existence index is a bounded, per-call filesystem walk (default cap 200,000 files, override via max_scan_files) -- a truncated or errored walk sets inconclusive=True on an UNKNOWN/UNREGISTERED result rather than reporting confident absence.
The generation counter in fallback_index_ledger.json is explicitly disposable -- losing it just resets the counter to 1, never a correctness issue.
No hosted/MCP call is made anywhere in this module -- fully local, matching the rest of this package.

supported_operations: run_completion_gate(docx_path, requirements=None, render_checker=None, skip_render_check=False) -> dict -- one fail-closed completion verdict: ready=True only when every hard structural check passes AND every set CompletionRequirements is satisfied
check_zip_integrity(raw) -- ZIP CRC-32, XML well-formedness, and required-part presence, all computed even after the first failure
enumerate_para_ids(document_xml) -- w14:paraId census split into body vs table-cell paragraphs, duplicate detection (the table-cell paraId gap class)
check_relationship_reachability(raw) -- every relationship target/rid/media file resolves; External TargetMode hyperlinks are never flagged
count_equations_and_captions(document_xml) -- m:oMath count, Caption-style paragraph count, SEQ field count
check_required_text(document_xml, required_texts, required_locators) -- plain substring assertions plus paraId-anchored (position-pinned) assertions

check_stale_source(docx_path, source_path=None, expected_source_sha256=None, expected_min_mtime=None) -- mtime ordering, source content-hash, and floor-timestamp staleness refusal (the 'stale worktree' guard)
CompletionRequirements -- declarative pass/fail knobs; structural corruption (bad CRC, malformed XML, duplicate paraIds, unresolved relationships) is always a hard failure, never a policy choice

Explicit render_report statuses (string-identical to extensions/meridian-docs/meridian_docs/render_gate.py's RENDERED/UNAVAILABLE_WITH_REASON/FAILED): RENDER_VERIFIED='render_verified', RENDER_UNVERIFIED='render_unverified', RENDER_UNAVAILABLE='render_unavailable', RENDER_FAILED='render_failed'
main(argv) -- CLI entry point: `python docx_completion_gate.py <docx_path> [--required-text ...] [--required-locator PARA_ID::TEXT] [--skip-render-check]`, exit 0/1
limitations: Structural checks are stdlib-only (zipfile + xml.etree.ElementTree) -- never full OOXML schema validation.

The ONE external render signal accepted is a real Word COM automation receipt, optionally delegated to meridian_docs.render_gate.check_word_com_render_receipt when that extension happens to be installed; its absence (non-Windows, no Word, extension not installed) is always RENDER_UNAVAILABLE, never silently folded into success.
Never raises for a bad/missing docx_path or malformed XML -- becomes a reported failure (ready=False with itemized reasons) instead.
Missing paraIds are counted, not treated as a hard failure -- some legitimately valid .docx files (never touched by Word 2010+) have none; duplicate paraIds are always a hard failure.

supported_operations: compare_figure_invariants(canonical, candidate) -> dict -- fail-closed comparison of two already-extracted FigureSlotPayload payloads (a FigureSlotPayload instance or a plain mapping with the same fields), returning one of five explicit verdicts

Explicit verdicts (never a bare bool): INVARIANT_HOLDS='invariant_holds' (bound source identical, numeric/text content unchanged -- only typography may differ), INVARIANT_VIOLATION='invariant_violation' (bound source identical but numeric and/or text content changed), SOURCE_MISMATCH='source_mismatch' (bound source differs, or was resolved only via content-hash relocation), AMBIGUOUS='ambiguous' (either slot's identity cannot be pinned to a single origin -- fails closed), NO_GENERATOR='no_generator' (neither a bound-source value nor any usable provenance signal exists for a slot -- distinct from AMBIGUOUS, never a crash)

FigureSlotPayload -- dataclass with bound_source (identity: {'kind','value'}, e.g. rid/resolved_path/generating_script -- never a caption string), numeric_values, text_content, typography (never compared for the verdict, only diffed for observability), caption_text (audit-only, never used for identity), provenance_type/provenance_candidates (optional, mirrors provenance_status.py's own vocabulary); to_dict()/from_dict() for lossless JSON round-tripping

PROVENANCE_EXACT/PROVENANCE_RELOCATED/PROVENANCE_AMBIGUOUS/PROVENANCE_DIRECTORY_FALLBACK/PROVENANCE_UNREGISTERED/PROVENANCE_UNKNOWN/PROVENANCE_STALE_BY_SCRIPT -- string-identical to extensions/meridian-outputs/meridian_outputs/provenance_status.py's own constants (and this package's output_provenance_gate.py, for the five that predate the relocation/ambiguity extension), so a caller threads either module's provenance_type straight into FigureSlotPayload with no translation
main(argv) -- CLI entry point: `python figure_invariant_gate.py <canonical.json> <candidate.json>`, exit 0 (INVARIANT_HOLDS) or 1 (any other verdict)
limitations: Operates ONLY on already-extracted payload dicts -- never reads a .docx, an outputs file, or calls the meridian-docs/meridian-outputs MCP extensions itself; a caller must resolve a figure slot's numeric/text content and bound-source identity before calling this gate.

Identity comparison is exact-match on (kind, value) only -- a RELOCATED (content-hash-confirmed-at-a-different-path) candidate is deliberately treated as SOURCE_MISMATCH rather than an equivalent match; this is a conservative fail-closed choice, not an oversight.

numeric_values/text_content equality is order-sensitive on the exact sequence a caller supplies -- reordering with no value change is reported under 'reordered' but still counts as INVARIANT_VIOLATION, since element order is part of the extracted-content contract the caller declares, not typography.

Hash-based identity ambiguity (two unrelated sources sharing an AMBIGUOUS/RELOCATED-with-multiple-candidates signal) is the caller's (provenance_status.py's) own known limitation, inherited here unmodified -- this gate only decides what to DO once that signal is present (fail closed), it does not resolve the ambiguity itself.

fallback_chain_example.comment: Illustrative set_capability_manifest() entry showing how a project would register this package as the fallback for a docx-editing capability whose primary tool is the meridian-docs MCP extension or a Word MCP tunnel slot. `capability` below is schema-checked by tools/meridian_fallbacks/tests/test_capability_parity.py against the REAL meridian.capability_manifest.normalize_capability() -- it must stay a genuinely valid capability entry (fields id/purpose/required_tools/fallback_chain/availability_policy/verification_command only; no 'capability_id', no stray 'comment' inside it), not merely illustrative JSON.

capability.purpose: Edit .docx files (insert content, insert images, apply reviewed patches) when authoring a document deliverable.
capability.verification_command: pixi run python -m pytest tools/meridian_fallbacks/tests/ -q --timeout=60 -p no:xdist

implementation_notes:
Copy/paste-ready usage:

from tools.meridian_fallbacks import (
    PatchManifest, apply_patch_manifest, insert_image, SafeOoxmlWriter,
)

# 1) Simple, single-shot edit (no manifest needed):
insert_image(
    "report.docx", image_path="chart.png",
    anchor_text="Figure 1", width_emu=4_572_000, height_emu=2_286_000,
)

# 2) Reviewable, transactional multi-op edit:
manifest = PatchManifest.create_from_file("report.docx")
image_bytes = open("chart.png", "rb").read()
op = manifest.add_operation(
    "insert_image", "word/document.xml", "insert Figure 1 chart",
    payload=image_bytes, metadata={"anchor_text": "Figure 1", "image_ext": "png"},
)
manifest.save("report.patch_manifest.json")  # durable, reviewable pointer

# ... later, possibly in a different process/session ...
manifest = PatchManifest.load("report.patch_manifest.json")
result = apply_patch_manifest(manifest, payloads={op.op_id: image_bytes})
assert result.success, result.error
# result.backup_path points at the pre-apply snapshot if a rollback is needed.

# 3) Local provenance fallback (no meridian-outputs MCP connection needed):
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "tools/meridian_fallbacks")
from output_provenance_gate import check_output_provenance
status = check_output_provenance("/abs/path/to/outputs", "/abs/path/to/outputs/results.csv")
# status["provenance_type"] in {EXACT, STALE_BY_SCRIPT, DIRECTORY_FALLBACK, UNREGISTERED, UNKNOWN}
# status["inconclusive"] is True only when the local scan did not converge -- never treat
# an inconclusive UNKNOWN as confirmed absence.
# Acceptance tests: tools/meridian_fallbacks/tests/test_output_provenance_gate.py

# 4) Figure-invariant gate (before claiming a figure typography edit complete):
from figure_invariant_gate import compare_figure_invariants, FigureSlotPayload
canonical = FigureSlotPayload(
    bound_source={"kind": "rid", "value": "rId50"},
    numeric_values=(1.0, 2.0, 3.0), text_content=("Convergence", "plot"),
)
candidate = FigureSlotPayload(
    bound_source={"kind": "rid", "value": "rId50"},
    numeric_values=(1.0, 2.0, 3.0), text_content=("Convergence", "plot"),
    typography={"font": "Times New Roman"},  # typography-only change
)
result = compare_figure_invariants(canonical, candidate)
assert result["verdict"] == "invariant_holds"
# Acceptance tests: tools/meridian_fallbacks/tests/test_figure_invariant_gate.py

# 5) Local DOCX completion gate (before claiming a docx-producing sprint item complete):
from docx_completion_gate import run_completion_gate, CompletionRequirements
report = run_completion_gate(
    "report.docx",
    CompletionRequirements(required_texts=["Executive Summary"], min_equation_count=1),
    skip_render_check=True,  # or omit to attempt a real Word/COM render receipt
)
assert report["ready"], report["reasons"]
# Acceptance tests: tools/meridian_fallbacks/tests/test_docx_completion_gate.py
# Cross-package parity + this manifest's own contract: tools/meridian_fallbacks/tests/test_capability_parity.py
